value.account:
WHAT CHANGED
- New auditor orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py (ResumeScopePath, ResumeProjectionIntegrityError, audit_scope, forensic/live current_step helpers), with resume_call_frame_audit.py (frame caller/alias/boundary/status/lineage checks), resume_retry_lineage.py (index_retry_lineage, next_unused_retry_frame_id) and resume_loop_progress.py (for_each and the four repeat_until forms). The auditor is pure over (bundle, state): no loading, checksums or file reads, no mutation.
- state_projection.py: ResumeProjectionValidationError, enumerate_resume_slots / resolve_resume_step_id / resolve_call_boundary, CallBoundaryProjection.import_alias, IterationStepKeyProjection.max_iterations (lowering.py supplies both). Candidates are built only from projection entries and the projection's loop/call APIs (qualified loop ids come from the existing runtime_step_id builders; nothing is parsed).
- state.py: record_workflow_checksum_mismatch / record_resume_projection_integrity_failure rewrite only status, error, updated_at on the raw state.json (unknown root fields survive, fail_run is not used).
- CLI resume: the observability override persist moved after load, root-checksum precheck, completed-run early return and the module-level audit_scope call; failure exits 1, prints the message, writes only the envelope. A failing session close cannot replace a persisted resume diagnostic.
- WorkflowExecutor: a structural root (state manager is a StateManager) rechecks the checksum (resume_root_guard.py) and then audits once, right before the prologue; call-frame executors get resume_scope_path from the caller and do not repeat it. _handle_control_flow returns _stop for the sticky error and records it as the run error; repeat_until/for_each promote it unwrapped and stop (typed and untyped for_each paths); finalization records supplemental failures (error null for ordinary cleanup failures) and lets a finalization-only projection error become the run error.
- CallExecutor: in resume mode one resolve_call_boundary per reached call, boundary alias selects the callee, completed-frame id collision check first, full frame audit, lineage-based selection (never mapping order; frame_id_with_overrides now only derives the fresh visit id), then checksum and bound-input validation, then failed predecessors (checksum + audit, recursive into open nested frames) and the running member's audit, all before _CallFrameStateManager exists. Child projection errors are returned unchanged, never call_failed.
- Observability: forensic current_step (failed run with projection/checksum error) is pending in build_status_snapshot, and ignored by the dashboard cursor/heartbeat and monitor heartbeat.
- Forked helpers did item 5 (orchestrator/loader_import_aliases.py, composed-node scan, hooked in WorkflowLoader._load_workflow before bundle construction) and item 8 (frontend_kind set in the Lisp lowering bundle builder, build_frontend_bundle no longer overwrites it, CallExecutor._is_workflow_lisp_target keys on it).
- specs/state.md section and specs/acceptance/index.md entries 201-209; tests/test_resume_projection_integrity.py (60 tests), tests/test_loader_import_alias_duplicates.py, tests/test_workflow_lisp_frontend_kind_provenance.py.

EXISTING TESTS I CHANGED (behaviour now required by the spec): the characterization tests from the previous commit (CLI/direct-executor mutation order, stale caller, callee-local corruption, ambiguity, current_step mismatch, malformed frame tests) now assert the new envelope; hand-built current_step fixtures gained step_id; three CLI observability tests with fake dict bundles patch resume.audit_scope; the adjudication sidecar test reports the recorded checksum because it edits the workflow by design; five Lisp hand-written-resume fixtures declare the historical step-granular lane (frontend_kind now marks them as Workflow Lisp); one lexical-restore test now expects invalid_loop_progress; five wcc structural goldens gained import_alias/max_iterations (verified as the only diff).
VERIFICATION: full suite 48 failed / 4788 passed vs 49 failed / 4720 passed at HEAD; the failing set is the same pre-existing one (two at72/adjudication timing tests flip between runs and pass alone). A CLI smoke (run, corrupt a step_id, resume exits 1 with the diagnostic and only the envelope written, repair, resume completes) passed.

CHOICES AND ALTERNATIVES
- Reason precedence for a row whose id is unknown and whose name is unowned: unknown_explicit_step_id wins over unclaimed_explicit_step_row; ambiguous row candidates report presentation_slot_mismatch (the spec has no separate reason). These are my readings of an ambiguous list.
- Terminal repeat_until forms with no loop row at all are accepted (lexical restore deliberately drops rows); a present but wrong row fails. I considered requiring the row and rejected it because it breaks the existing restore flow.
- Active repeat_until history must be exactly range(current_iteration), the strictest reading of valid prior history.
- Considered a planner-owned audit and an executor-only audit; discarded because the CLI needs to fail before observability/session writes and the executor needs to cover direct resume. Considered skipping the audit for non-bundle objects to keep fake-bundle tests untouched; discarded as silent defensive code.
- Retry ids: only a tail ::retry::<n> is a marker; a marker embedded before a '.' (nested frame inside a retried parent) is part of the base id, so legitimate nested frames are not rejected.

NOT COVERED / RISKS
- Nothing is committed. The resolver treats each loop's own nested keys only; loops nested inside loop bodies were not exercised. Completed nested frames inside failed predecessors are not checksum-audited. The exact reason for some overlapping cases (above) and whether hidden tests expect the old call_resume_state_invalid details for malformed frames on the root path are guesses. Module-size and complexity limits: new modules are under 500 lines, but calls.py (already over) grew. No docs/index or capability-matrix update was made. Three-attempt reassessment was not needed.
value.summary: Resume now audits every persisted identity of each scope it executes against the current projection and fails closed with one non-routable diagnostic before any mutation or effect, plus the YAML import-alias checks, typed Workflow Lisp provenance, specs and tests.

value.account: Checked: the new integrity, loader-alias and frontend-kind test modules plus resume-command and subworkflow tests pass (175). The full suite shows 47 failed / 4789 passed. The previous attempt reported 48 failed, and the semantic-IR failures also occur at baseline (3 fail with my stash applied). Verified the auditor modules contain no forbidden migration/receipt/cache identifiers, that audit_scope is a module-level name in calls, executor and the resume command, that new modules are under 500 lines, and that resolve_call_boundary is used for reached calls. I did not change anything: no defect turned up that would justify a rewrite. Not covered: I did not re-verify each of the twelve reasons' field/offending/candidate_count values or every ordering envelope by hand; I relied on the existing 60 behavioural tests. Known risks from the earlier attempt remain: some overlapping-reason precedence choices are interpretations, loops nested in loop bodies are not exercised, completed nested frames inside failed predecessors are not checksum-audited, calls.py is over 500 lines, and nothing is committed.
